review: 1:1–2 and 2:1–2 both break the sentence mid-clause (لَا بُدَّ أَنْ يَأْتِي / مَنْ مَاتَ …), and the Hebrew keeps the break ('He must come who / died'), so line 2:1 ends on the relative particle as the Arabic ends on مَنْ.

2:4 כַּאֲשֶׁר עָלָה בֶעָנָן — Acts 1:9–11 (נִשָּׂא … וְעָנָן קִבְּלוּהוּ) with Dan 7:13; the ascent in the cloud is kept as the ground of the return, since the Arabic كَمَا مَضَى مَعَ الْغَمَام is an argument from the first coming to the second.

3:2 צִבְאוֹת קֹדֶשׁ — the Arabic أَجْنَادِ وَالْأَمْلَاك is 'hosts and angels'; the Hebrew keeps both classes with the construct צִבְאוֹת קֹדֶשׁ (holy hosts) rather than collapsing them into 'angels'.

3:4 מִכִּפַּת הַשָּׁמָיִם — the Arabic مِنْ قُبَّةِ الْأَفْلَاك is the vault of the spheres; כִּפָּה is post-biblical for dome, accepted here because the Arabic's image is architectural (the sky as a vault) and 'from heaven' would lose it.

4:2–4 עֲטָרוֹת / כִּסְאוֹת — the Arabic نَبْقَى مُكَلَّلِين … عَلَى عُرُوشِ الْمَجْدِ is Rev 3:21 (וְיָשַׁבְתִּי … עַל־כִּסְאִי) with 1 Cor 6:3; the thrones and crowns are kept as two separate promises, as the Arabic keeps them.
